title: Trace the URL shortener under pressure
description: Switch scenarios to see which components enter the request path, where failures are isolated, and what remains available. Select any component for its responsibility.

nodes.label: Browser
nodes.detail: Requests a compact link and follows the redirect response to the destination owner.

nodes.label: Edge + routing
nodes.detail: Terminates TLS, applies DDoS and coarse abuse controls, and routes the request to a healthy redirect region.

nodes.label: Redirect service
nodes.detail: Validates the code, checks local policy, resolves the destination, and returns the HTTP redirect without waiting for analytics.

nodes.label: Distributed cache
nodes.detail: Serves popular code-to-destination mappings in memory. Misses fall through to the authoritative store with bounded concurrency.

nodes.label: Mapping store
nodes.detail: Owns durable code uniqueness, destination and policy data. It must survive cache misses but should not receive every redirect.

nodes.label: Durable stream
nodes.detail: Buffers compact redirect events outside the response path so a slow analytics consumer cannot increase redirect latency.

nodes.label: Stream processor
nodes.detail: Filters bots, applies privacy rules, and builds bounded time-window aggregates for reporting.

nodes.label: Analytical store
nodes.detail: Serves owner dashboards and long-range analysis without competing with redirect lookups in the mapping store.

nodes.label: Create API
nodes.detail: Authenticates the caller, validates the destination shape, and enforces account, tenant, and anonymous quotas.

nodes.label: Safety check
nodes.detail: Rejects known harmful destinations and sends uncertain cases through stricter policy without touching the redirect path.

nodes.label: Code allocator
nodes.detail: Allocates generated codes from non-overlapping ranges or conditionally reserves a requested custom alias.

scenarios.label: Cache hit
scenarios.summary: The dominant request stays on the short path: edge, stateless redirect service, and distributed cache. Analytics leaves asynchronously.
scenarios.result: The destination is returned without mapping-store I/O; a slow analytics consumer cannot delay the redirect.

scenarios.label: Cache miss
scenarios.summary: The service checks the authoritative mapping store only after the cache misses, then repopulates the hot mapping for later requests.
scenarios.result: The redirect is slower but remains correct. Miss coalescing and fallback limits prevent a hot code from stampeding storage.

scenarios.label: Create link
scenarios.summary: Creation is a separate, lower-volume path that performs safety checks and commits unique code ownership before publishing the mapping.
scenarios.result: The API returns success only after durable ownership is committed; cache publication makes the new link ready for redirects.

scenarios.label: Cache outage
scenarios.summary: The cache is unavailable, so controlled traffic bypasses it. The redirect tier sheds abuse and caps store fallback concurrency.
scenarios.result: Availability is reduced but bounded fallback protects the mapping store from becoming the next failure.

scenarios.label: Analytics outage
scenarios.summary: The event pipeline is unavailable while the correctness path remains healthy. Redirects continue and events may be dropped or buffered locally.
scenarios.result: Redirect latency and availability remain unchanged because analytics is explicitly outside the response path.
